items.name: Marina / harbor place anchor
notes: Shared POI family concerns reusable classification/treatment semantics; it does not imply shared bespoke geometry.
Torrevieja port treatment was upgraded city-side to bespoke-complex; shared family remains classification/treatment semantics only and never implies shared harbor geometry.
Cartagena Phase 2 sharpens harbor/marina site relationships; shared POI semantics never imply common port geometry.

items.name: Urban park
notes: Shared POI family concerns reusable classification/treatment semantics; it does not imply shared bespoke geometry.
Torrevieja re-research removed Molino del Agua from this shared urban-park family: official evidence identifies it as a protected dune-and-pine natural landscape, not primarily an urban park.
Benidorm Phase 2 refines Parc de l’Aigüera as an authored linear urban-structure/transition element, not an interchangeable green patch.
Málaga Phase 2 removes the Guadalhorce estuary from “urban park”: regional evidence identifies it as a protected natural wetland/estuary.

items.name: Urban / settlement beach
notes: Shared POI family concerns reusable classification/treatment semantics; it does not imply shared bespoke geometry.
Alicante now has at least two materially different beach anchors: central Postiguet and the long northeastern Playa de San Juan; shared classification does not imply identical spatial treatment.
Benidorm demonstrates that shared “urban beach” treatment needs scale/edge subtypes: two major linear beach systems plus the much smaller Mal Pas cove.
Cartagena Phase 2 adds Mar Menor urban-beach variants whose identity depends on promenade, nautical and rail/transport relationships rather than skyline towers.

Málaga demonstrates three materially different urban-beach contexts inside one city: central civic/tourism foreground, traditional promenade/fishing barrio, and active maritime-neighborhood beach edge.
